subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: For aborted/no-output GitHub Copilot `anthropic-messages` isolated cron runs, should OpenClaw add transport-level idle/progress failure first, or classify this aborted result shape as fallback-safe?
rationale: Both choices can fix the user-visible hang, but result-level fallback after an abort can replay work and requires an owner decision about side-effect safety.

options.title: Prefer transport-level failure proof
options.body: Add or prove a Copilot Anthropic first-token idle/progress timeout so the provider path fails before any ambiguous partial agent work can be replayed.

options.title: Make aborted no-output fallback-safe
options.body: Allow model fallback for a narrow aborted/no-output result shape after proving no tools, text, or delivery evidence were committed.

options.title: Keep only cron error classification
options.body: Accept that aborted Copilot Claude cron runs now report errors, but do not attempt automatic fallback without stronger replay-safety proof.

recommendation.title: Prefer transport-level failure proof
recommendation.body: Add or prove a Copilot Anthropic first-token idle/progress timeout so the provider path fails before any ambiguous partial agent work can be replayed.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is centered on the GitHub Copilot provider routing and transport boundary that steipete introduced and still appears connected to in current history.
